description:
## Problem
The generation-estimate re-measure (#4446, run folder `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/generation-estimate/remeasure-20261122/`) found that TPC-H data generation takes about 4–5 s at both SF 0.01 and SF 0.1, so small scales gain nothing from their smaller size. Cause, with evidence in that folder (`dbgen_direct`, `dbgen_fixed` and `par/` logs, load below 3, Apple M4, 10 cores): the stock dbgen builds a fixed 300 MiB text pool (`TEXT_POOL_SIZE`, `_sources/tpc-h/dbgen/text.c:89`) before writing its first comment, in every process, whatever the scale or table. One `dbgen -vf -s 0.01` takes 1.57 s; every single-table run at SF 0.01 takes 1.40–1.49 s; peak RSS is about 316 MB. BenchBox passes `{"parallel": cpu_cores}` (`benchmark_loader.py`), so the CLI starts 10 chunk processes that each pay the cost: an SF 0.01 run used 20 s of CPU in 4.7 s wall. In-process timings: parallel 1 = 2.60 s, 4 = 1.63 s, 10 = 2.29 s at SF 0.01; 2.92 / 1.89 / 2.74 s at SF 0.1. The rest is about 1 s of uv and CLI start-up, a 0.2 s sleep and `sync` (0.2–0.35 s).
Prior art: #4316 already runs dbgen once for compressed data at SF ≤ 1. State which compression mode the re-measure used and whether the fix extends #4316's rule to uncompressed output.

## Change
Investigate, then propose to the owner: choose the number of dbgen chunk processes from scale and core count at small scales, so small-scale generation stops paying the pool cost many times. Find where the process count and the chunked-versus-single-file layout are chosen (benchmark loader, TPC-H generator, #4316's rule). Do not change dbgen's text pool.

## Decision gates
- STOP before implementing: present the measured options (process count per scale, wall and CPU time, file layout effect) to the owner in a choice dialog; the default process count and the file layout are owner decisions.
- STOP if any option changes generated data: the sorted row content of every TPC-H table at SF 0.01 and 0.1 must hash equal to develop's (compare rows, not files, because the chunk layout may change).
- Measure on an idle host only (1-minute load below 3), through `make heavy-run`; if admission is refused or free disk would fall below 50 GiB, stop and report.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the owner's chosen rule implemented; row-content hashes at SF 0.01 and 0.1 equal develop's; before/after wall and CPU time at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 in the pull request, with SF 0.01 and 0.1 wall time below the parallel=4 figures above; `benchbox/core/generation_estimate.json` re-measured if its figures move by more than 10%; a test pins the process-count rule at its scale boundaries. A blanket cap of one process fails (it is slower than four).
Fail: data differs, figures not measured, or a default changed without the owner's choice.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
